opportunities.title: Recover the front door: clean roofing site, quote intake, and a single correct Google profile link
opportunities.problem: The brand domain biondoroofing.com now serves a Thai-language slot-game page that mimics a Google Play listing, with no phone, address, services or navigation. The Google Business Profile (4.9 stars) still uses that domain as its website field, so every search or Maps click on the brand lands on gambling spam. There is no reachable quote form, no click-to-call page, and nothing machine-readable for AI assistants to quote from - and the firm's own hours, address and phone contradict each other across Google, Birdeye and ProvenExpert.
evidence: Desktop and phone (390 px) loads of biondoroofing.com render a Thai slot-game page titled สล็อตโรม่าทดลอง with zero business information: https://biondoroofing.com/

The Google Business Profile 'Biondo Contracting-Roofing Specialists' is rated 4.9 but its website field points at that same domain: https://www.google.com/maps/search/Biondo+Contracting+Roofing+Specialists+Monroe+Township+NJ

An Internet Archive capture from 2026-04-20 still shows the normal roofing homepage, which published license 13VH01287400, so legitimate content was live roughly seven months ago: https://web.archive.org/web/20260420032126/https://biondoroofing.com/

RDAP shows the domain was registered 2010 and is paid through 2030-12-07, registrar-locked at GoDaddy - the loss is a hosting/CMS compromise on a domain the owner still controls, not an expiry squat: https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/biondoroofing.com

How prospects used to convert: a WPForms 'CONTACT US TODAY' block on the homepage and on a dedicated free-estimate page, plus a published info@biondoroofing.com address - all now unreachable: https://web.archive.org/web/20250518163153/https://biondoroofing.com/free-roofing-or-siding-estimate-new-jersey/

Front-door inconsistencies confirmed by an earlier browser review: two addresses (38 Spotswood Ave Monroe vs 163 Fresh Ponds Rd East Brunswick), at least two phone numbers, and hours advertised as midnight/24-7 on some surfaces versus Mon-Fri 8:30-7:30 on Birdeye; agent-readiness scored findable 2, answerable 0, bookable 0: https://birdeye.com/biondo-contracting-east-brunswick-nj-149586765701051
opportunities.agent_design: Two phases. (1) Containment and recovery: with the owner's GoDaddy/host credentials, take a malware and credential audit of the compromised WordPress install, kill the injected content, keep the domain and mail, and stand up a clean site (static or managed WordPress) on the same domain with https, redirects, and preserved URLs for the archived service pages. Publish the essentials in both human and machine-readable form: services (asphalt replacement and repair, flat/low-slope membrane, VELUX skylights, flashing, ventilation, siding), the town-by-town service area, one canonical phone, one address, license 13VH01287400, RoofingContractor/LocalBusiness schema and an hours block. (2) Front-door agent: an intake agent behind a quote form with roof-photo upload and a short structured questionnaire (roof type, leak vs replacement, town, age, insurance involvement) that acknowledges in minutes, qualifies against the service-area list, and either offers an inspection window or escalates an active leak to Sam by SMS. A listing agent then repoints the Google profile website field, unifies name-address-phone across Google, Birdeye, ProvenExpert and BBB, and keeps a nightly watch on the domain (resolves to Biondo content, valid certificate, profile link intact) so a re-compromise pages a human the same day. Human approval: Sam signs off copy, service-area list, any published price ranges, and every booked slot.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A Wix/Square-style builder does not recover a compromised WordPress install, audit for injected redirects or fix the poisoned indexed title. It also does not repoint the Google Business Profile, reconcile four directories, generate schema an AI assistant can read, or monitor the domain for re-compromise. The value here is diagnosis (hosting/CMS compromise versus expired domain), cross-platform listing surgery, and a persistent intake agent - none of which is a subscription a roofer can self-serve.

impact_estimate.range: Restores the only online intake channel that was carrying quotes until April 2026. Modeled gross booked work: 1-2 recovered booked replacements per month at a 25-40% close rate on NJ average installed prices of about $9,000 (flat/EPDM) to $12,500 (architectural shingle) = roughly $27k-$120k/yr in gross contract value, not margin. Plan on the low end: pre-compromise web lead volume is unmeasured.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes current web lead flow is zero because the live page contains no form or phone (verified). Assumes the 4.9-star Google profile and 172-review history still generate clicks that today dead-end on spam. Assumes 1-2 estimate requests per month are actually recovered and that 25-40% close, which is a planning assumption, not a measured rate. Also ignores admin savings from the form (a web inquiry replaces a 15-20 minute phone call worth about $6-8 at the NJ customer-service-representative median of $47,740/2,080hr = $22.95/hr, per https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v1/timeseries/data/OEUS340000000000043405113). Any actual value depends on how fast the domain, Google link and listings are fixed.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: malware/credential audit and containment decision, clean 5-7 page site live on biondoroofing.com (home, services, service area, about/license, free-estimate page with photo-upload form, contact), schema and machine-readable business facts published, Google profile website field repointed, one canonical phone/address/hours set applied to Google, Birdeye and ProvenExpert, and a daily domain-integrity check emailing Sam. Deliverable: a working, monitored front door with a form that produces a job sheet per inquiry.

opportunities.title: AI intake and missed-call recovery for a phone-only roofer whose owner is on the roof
opportunities.problem: After the site loss, the only way to reach Biondo is to call one number. The firm self-declares 8 employees, the owner personally inspects roofs and runs crews, and there is no answering service, chat, booking widget or CRM found on any reachable surface - while the published hours disagree with each other (Google shows open to midnight, archived pages claim 24/7, Birdeye says Mon-Fri 8:30-7:30 and closed Sunday). Tear-off days and storm weeks are exactly when calls go unanswered, and the repair/callback traffic visible in reviews makes that a steady stream, not a seasonal one.
evidence: Intake is now a single channel - call (732) 257-2926 from the Google profile; no reachable form, email capture or booking flow exists because the domain serves spam: https://www.google.com/maps/search/Biondo+Contracting+Roofing+Specialists+Monroe+Township+NJ

Contradictory published hours (midnight on Google, 24/7 in archived schema, 8:30-7:30 Mon-Fri on Birdeye) mean a caller cannot know when a person answers: https://birdeye.com/biondo-contracting-east-brunswick-nj-149586765701051

Site schema declares numberOfEmployees 8, and reviews describe the same owner inspecting roofs and being on site - no desk staff visible: https://web.archive.org/web/20250518163153/https://biondoroofing.com/

Reviews credit 'Sam'/'Sam Biondo' as the owner who personally inspects and runs the crews, i.e. the decision-maker is also the intake bottleneck: https://birdeye.com/biondo-contracting-east-brunswick-nj-149586765701051

Repair and post-install callback work is normal traffic (leak re-checks, a damaged shingle fixed the next day, plywood replaced at no charge), so incoming calls mix emergencies, warranty checks and sales: https://birdeye.com/biondo-contracting-east-brunswick-nj-149586765701051
No chat widget, booking widget, customer portal or CRM signal on any reachable surface; the only live owned property is the Google profile: https://biondo-contracting.webflow.io/
opportunities.agent_design: A voice-and-SMS intake agent on a business number that the office can hand off to and pull back from. It answers when nobody picks up (after hours, during tear-offs, weekends), opening with the roof-specific script: active leak or storm damage, repair vs full replacement, roof type (shingle, flat/EPDM, skylight, siding), town, roof age, insurance involvement, and a photo request by SMS. It qualifies against the published town-by-town service area, offers inspection windows from Sam's real availability, and escalates anything urgent (active interior leak, missing shingles after a storm, tarp request) straight to Sam by SMS with a transcript summary. Every call and form becomes a structured job sheet on a simple lead board with a 7 a.m. digest of new leads, unanswered calls and follow-ups due. It also chases stalled items: estimate requests with no reply, quotes sent with no decision, and inspection appointments to confirm. Human approval: Sam sees and can override every booking; prices, scope and any commitment are drafted by the agent but approved by Sam before they reach a customer.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot answer a ringing phone, cannot hand off mid-call when Sam picks up, cannot enforce a town-level service-area filter against a calendar, and cannot run an escalation policy for emergencies. Wiring telephony (number portability, voicemail, SMS), a calendar, a lead board and photo intake together - with transcripts and homeowner addresses kept in a private store - is integration and reliability work, not a chat window.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 10-20 hours a week of owner/office intake and callback time returned to estimating and job supervision, worth about $12k-$24k/yr at the NJ customer-service-representative median ($47,740/2,080hr = $22.95/hr) - or about $14k-$27k/yr at the NJ dispatcher median ($54,590). Explicitly NOT counted: booked-job revenue from recovered after-hours calls, which cannot be estimated from public evidence.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 15-30 inbound inquiries a week at a 172-review residential roofer and that most after-hours and in-day calls currently go to voicemail or unanswered (inference from phone-only intake plus an owner who is on roofs; call logs were not available). Assumes 15-20 minutes of admin per inquiry (capture, qualification, scheduling, callback notes). The +14% issues-resolved-per-hour figure from NBER working paper w31161 (5,179 customer-support agents) is used only as a directional analogue for the booking desk - it is a customer-support study, not a roofing measurement, so no throughput percentage is claimed here.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: one business number with after-hours and overflow answering plus SMS, a 10-question roof qualification flow, town-level service-area check, inspection-slot booking against Sam's calendar, emergency escalation to Sam's phone, a lead board with daily digest, and two weeks of call transcripts reviewed jointly to tune the script. Deliverable: measured call capture (calls answered, after-hours calls captured, inspection slots booked) with Sam approving every booking.

opportunities.title: Agent-built job record and warranty system so leak callbacks are resolved from evidence, not memory
opportunities.problem: Biondo's reputational edge is owner-led, no-hidden-fee work documented by word of mouth, but there is no CRM, portal or job-record system anywhere in evidence - crews finish a tear-off in one to two days and the knowledge of what went under the shingles, which decking was replaced and when the manufacturer warranty started lives with Sam. Reviews already show the cost: free plywood replacements and next-day return visits handled as goodwill, plus one complaint that the firm did not stand behind its work after payment. With manufacturer certifications (Owens Corning, CertainTeed, GAF) and no visible warranty registration or photo trail, covered failures are paid for twice and disputes are argued from memory.
evidence: No CRM, customer portal or job-record signal found on any reachable surface; only the Google profile is live: https://www.google.com/maps/search/Biondo+Contracting+Roofing+Specialists+Monroe+Township+NJ

Reviews describe post-install callbacks handled ad hoc - leak re-checks, a damaged shingle fixed the next day, plywood replaced at no charge despite a contract fee: https://birdeye.com/biondo-contracting-east-brunswick-nj-149586765701051

A minority complaint alleges the firm did not return calls after payment, i.e. callback handling is a live reputational risk (one reviewer, not a pattern): https://birdeye.com/biondo-contracting-east-brunswick-nj-149586765701051

Manufacturer positioning as Owens Corning / CertainTeed / GAF certified with its own employees (not subcontractors), which is exactly the basis for extended manufacturer warranties that require registration and documentation: https://web.archive.org/web/20260420032126/https://biondoroofing.com/

Service mix includes flat/low-slope membrane, VELUX skylights, flashing around chimneys and HVAC, seamless gutters and siding - each with different warranty terms and failure modes that a record system would need to distinguish: https://birdeye.com/biondo-contracting-east-brunswick-nj-149586765701051

Old site already ran WordPress with GA4 and WPForms, so there is a domain and a web stack to hang an internal tool on once it is cleaned: https://web.archive.org/web/20250518163153/https://biondoroofing.com/
opportunities.agent_design: An agent-built job-record tool for an 8-person crew, not an enterprise FSM suite. Triggers: a job is booked (from the intake agent or manually) - the agent creates a record keyed to the property address, pulls the estimate and scope, and opens a photo checklist by stage (tear-off, decking, underlayment/ice-and-water, flashing details, skylight curb, completion, gutters). Crews shoot photos on their phones; the agent tags them, reads material and underlayment labels off the images, and files the set against the job. On completion it assembles a one-page 'roof passport' - materials, layers removed, decking sheets replaced, skylight models, warranty start and end dates - submits the manufacturer warranty registration, and texts the homeowner a link/QR to their record. When a callback arrives (phone, form or text), the agent retrieves the passport, checks date against warranty terms and the documented install, and drafts either a no-charge warranty visit or a paid repair scope for Sam to approve, with the photo evidence attached. It also queues a reminder at the warranty midpoint and at the 10-year mark. Human approval: Sam (or a crew lead he names) decides coverage on every callback and approves every customer message; coverage decisions are never automated, and there is no accusation logic anywhere in the system.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Nothing in evidence comes close to this out of the box: the firm has no CRM, no photo app and no warranty register, and the pieces have to be built and joined - phone-capture pipeline, image tagging, document reading, a property-keyed database, SMS links and warranty-registration rules per manufacturer. A generic photo app stores pictures but cannot answer 'is this leak covered on this roof' or assemble a defensible record. This is internal-software and integration work with a human sign-off gate, which is what makes it auditable if a dispute or insurance claim arises.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $3k-$12k/yr, mostly from fewer unbilled return visits and faster warranty claims: 1-2 goodwill callbacks a month at 2-4 crew-hours each is about $1.5k-$3.5k/yr of direct labor at the NJ roofer median ($76,600/2,080hr = $36.83/hr), plus 2-4 hours a week of owner record-keeping and callback triage at the NJ first-line-supervisor median ($105,510/2,080hr = $50.73/hr), about $5k-$10k/yr. Excludes any recovered manufacturer material credit, which is real but unquantified.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes the callback volume visible in public reviews (leak re-checks, next-day shingle repair, free plywood) continues at roughly 1-2 a month and that half of those are currently absorbed as unbilled labor - inference from review text, since no job-cost data is public. Assumes the owner currently spends 2-4 hours a week on records and callback coordination. Deliberately does not model revenue from higher close rates on callbacks; the case rests on labor avoided and dispute defensibility.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: a property-keyed job record with a phone photo checklist, 3-4 live jobs documented end to end, auto-generated roof passports with warranty dates and manufacturer registration submitted for those jobs, a homeowner link/QR, and a callback workflow that surfaces the passport with draft response for Sam's approval. Deliverable: documented pilot jobs plus a 30-day measure of time spent on records and callbacks versus the current baseline.

lead_score.rationale: Pain is near-maximal and verified from multiple independent sources: a 4.9-star Google profile pointing at a Thai gambling clone, a business that self-declares 8 staff, 172 reviews on Birdeye showing real job volume, phone-only intake, contradictory hours and two addresses in circulation. Fit is strong - G plus A cover the documented gaps, D fits an operator with no CRM at all. Ability to pay is the soft spot: an owner-operated 8-person residential roofer in a high-wage state plausibly clears seven figures of revenue at NJ installed prices, but cash position, current job backlog and appetite for software spend are unknown, and the site has been broken for roughly seven months without a visible fix, which may mean low urgency or simply that nobody told him. Ease is middling: one known decision-maker (Sam) and a clear first deliverable, but the engagement starts with a compromised-hosting recovery that depends on his registrar/host access, and a half-finished Webflow page suggests a rebuild may already be in someone else's hands. Strategic value is high and repeatable: 'hijacked brand domain + phone-only intake' is a pattern that thousands of small roofing and home-service firms share, and the domain-integrity watch, listing repair and intake agent are all reusable assets. No physical/edge (E) opportunity was included: avenues.json is not in this folder, the observable footprint is crews and residential roofs with no shop floor, inventory, dock or equipment-monitoring signal, and anything camera-based here would drift toward theft/surveillance, which under N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2 would need a licensed alarm contractor and adds legal overhead for little operational gain. Evidence quality note: the front-door and intake facts are strong and directly sourced; the dollar ranges are modeled from wage benchmarks and a vendor cost guide and should be presented to the owner as planning assumptions, not forecasts.
lead_score.evidence_note: Front-door and intake evidence is direct and multiply sourced; impact ranges are modeled, not measured.
